Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the product overview last week. We’re moving ahead with an internal eval and procurement needs a clear breakdown of costs for a private deployment (VPC / on-prem). Specifically we need: 

- Licensing model: per-node vs per-seat, examples for our estimated footprint (6 inference nodes, 100k tokens/day)
- Annual platform fee: what it covers and how it’s amortized
- Support tiers and SLAs (Standard vs Premier) and associated response/oncall commitments

I’ve attached a short SOW template outlining our deliverables. Could you send a written pricing sheet and a proposal by EOD tomorrow?

Ben — can you draft the numbers (ballpark) and attach the fee breakout? Marissa/Laura — help tighten legal/proc wording for SOW. I’ll own the reply to Elena.

Mateo — draft below with numbers we can stand behind for procurement. I kept the math conservative so we have room to flex. I attached an XLS with line items.

--- Price summary (annualized, US list pricing) ---
1) License (inference nodes): $15,000 per inference node / year (includes runtime optimizations and model hosting license)
  - Example: 6 nodes => $90,000 / year
2) Platform fee (annual): $40,000 / year (control plane, telemetry retention 90 days, model catalog, team seats x5)
3) Support tiers (annual add-on):
  - Standard: $12,000 / year (business hours, 24-hour P1 response)
  - Premier: $36,000 / year (24/7 P1, 4-hour P1 response, quarterly SRE sync)
4) Implementation retainer (one-time): $25,000 (estimated 6 weeks onboarding + 10 days dedicated engineering)

Subtotal (example for ZenHealth baseline):
  License (6 nodes): $90,000
  Platform fee: $40,000
  Support (Standard): $12,000
  Implementation retainer: $25,000
  ----
  Total year-1 (list): $167,000

Discount / Migration credit options we can offer: 
- Option A (12-month commit): 10% discount on combined license+platform fee for year-1 + $10k migration credit applied to implementation retainer.
- Option B (12-month commit + 6m engineering retainer prepay): 15% discount on combined license+platform fee + $20k migration credit.
- Option C (24-month commit): 20% discount on combined license+platform fee; migration credit negotiable depending on engineering hours.

Rationale: credits tied to prepay/commit reduce our churn risk and offset initial onboarding cost for the customer.

I attached Platform_Fee_Breakdown.xlsx with line-items, SLAs, and feature mapping for Standard vs Premier.

If you want, we can present Option A as a starting point and hold Option B as the negotiable sweetener.

—Ben

Attachment: Platform_Fee_Breakdown.xlsx

1) Can we get a line that clarifies what the platform fee covers around data residency and audit logs (we need 1 year retention for certain audit trails)?
2) The implementation retainer looks high relative to the migration credit offered: would Redwood consider applying the credit directly to the first-year platform fee rather than the retainer? That helps our CAPEX vs OPEX budgeting.

Procurement wants a DocuSign-ready SOW and an itemized invoice for the initial payment. Can you get that to us by EOD PST?

Hi Elena — appreciate the quick feedback. We can accommodate your asks; summary below and I’ve attached a DocuSign-ready SOW and the line-item sheet.

Responses to your questions: 
1) Platform fee & audit/data residency: We can extend telemetry retention to 365 days as an addendum to the platform fee for an incremental $6,000 / year. Audit logs for compliance export via S3 are included; the addendum covers storage and retention policy support.

2) Credit application: We can re-scope Option A so the $10k migration credit applies as a credit against the first-year platform fee (so you see it in OPEX line items). Option B’s $20k credit can be split 50/50 between platform fee and retainer by request.

3) Engineering retainer invoicing: Retainer is invoiced up-front as a professional services prepay. Unused hours do not roll over beyond 90 days but can be converted to delivery milestones in the SOW at our mutual agreement. We’ve added a clause to that effect in the attached SOW.

Attached: ZenHealth_SOW_v1.pdf (updated with DocuSign fields), Platform_Fee_Breakdown.xlsx (updated with 365-day retention line), and a draft invoice example.

Next steps: If that looks good, I’ll send the DocuSign package (SOW + invoice) and we can target a 30-day execution cadence from signature. If procurement wants a slightly larger credit we can escalate a one-time executive approval — let me know the target and I’ll route it.

Best,
